_readme: Reported revenue disclosures. One entry per disclosure, never per article. value_b is USD billions annualized unless kind says otherwise. qualifier: '>' threshold, '~' approximate, '=' stated. obs_date is the date used for plotting; obs_label keeps the real precision. Grades: A company announcement read directly; B original financial journalism read directly; C read via republication or secondary report; D unresolved, excluded. forecasts holds published expectations; they are shown for comparison and never used to fit anything.

grades.C: Republication or secondary report; original not inspected
grades.D: Unresolved or insufficiently traced; excluded from calibration

anchors.excerpt: approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025
anchors.note: Retrospective figure published in April; averaging window and partner gross/net basis not specified.

anchors.excerpt: Today, our run-rate revenue is $14 billion
anchors.note: Not a confirmed February month-end value.
Claude Code product run rate. A subset of A02; never add to the company total.

anchors.excerpt: recently surpassed $19 billion in run-rate revenue
anchors.note: Attributed to people familiar with the matter; observation day imprecise.

anchors.excerpt: Our run-rate revenue has now surpassed $30 billion
anchors.note: Threshold; not an April month-end value.

anchors.obs_label: Earlier in May 2026 (plotted at publication date)
anchors.excerpt: our run-rate revenue crossed $47 billion earlier this month

anchors.note: Underlying Bloomberg report not inspected; accounting basis unresolved.

anchors.source: Axios, citing NYT (read via Yahoo Finance republication)
anchors.excerpt: pacing to generate more than $100 billion in annual revenue
anchors.note: NYT original not inspected. Axios describes a current pace, up 50% from two months earlier and 10x the end of 2025, consistent with A07 and A01. Bloomberg's account of the same report says Anthropic 'is expected to generate more than $100 billion in annualized revenue this year', so the figure may be an expectation for 2026 rather than a September observation. Recorded as the latest figure with that caveat.
ARR comparison across years; exact annualization convention not provided.
Derived: the announcement states $2B revenue per month; x12 gives a rounded $24B annualized reference. Monthly averaging window unstated.

anchors.excerpt: annualized revenue run rate has hit $40 billion
anchors.note: Observation date ambiguous (July vs mid-August). Superseded as the latest OpenAI figure by A20.

anchors.excerpt: $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate
anchors.note: Advertising segment only; do not add to an already inclusive total.

anchors.excerpt: up from $5.7 billion in the first quarter
anchors.note: Recognized quarterly revenue, not a run rate. x4 = $22.8B quarterly-average pace; consistency check only.

anchors.excerpt: $6.7 billion in the three months ended in June
anchors.note: Recognized quarterly revenue, not a run rate. x4 = $26.8B quarterly-average pace; consistency check only.

anchors.source: Bloomberg, citing Axios (read via Yahoo Finance republication)
anchors.excerpt: on track to generate annualized revenue of nearly $70 billion
anchors.note: 'Nearly' is recorded as approximately $70B. Axios original not accessible. Growth attributed in part to AI coding software. Secondary coverage also reports enterprise sales more than doubling since July; that wording was not inspected.

context.claim: Business is the majority of revenue; July run-rate growth 20% month over month
context.note: Mix and growth cross-check; business includes more than seats.
Historical mix cross-check; not additive to total.

context.claim: Approximately 80% of revenue from business/enterprise customers
context.note: Customer mix, not an API billing split; stale for mid-2026.
Adoption evidence only, not partner revenue share.

context.claim: 2025 revenue nearly $4.6B: $3.8B usage-based, $789M subscriptions. 47% of sales went through Amazon and Google, up from 32% in 2024 and 11% in 2023
context.note: Reuters on the confidential IPO prospectus, read via Yahoo Finance. The only filing-based mix data for either lab; it sets Anthropic's split. Microsoft's channel is not in the 47%. Amazon and Google kept about 16 cents per dollar of those sales.

context.claim: Run rate up 70% since the start of the third quarter; business-to-business revenue more than doubled over the same period
context.note: PYMNTS citing Axios. With business already the majority in August (A10), this caps consumer plus advertising below half of revenue. Conflict: 70% growth since 1 July implies about $41B then, while A09 and A10 (about $40B in mid-August after 20% growth in July) imply about $33B. Not used as a calibration point for that reason.
